SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK CQL-05: CQL - Type Operators - Structural. Test these items: As<T>(argument); Children(argument); Convert to<T>(argument); Descendants(argument); Is<T>(argument).

For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.summary: Structural type targets were not validated consistently for `is`, `as`, and `convert`; unknown targets could silently translate.
`List<T>` and `Interval<T>` type specifiers were not first-class operands for structural `is` and `as`.
Static structural type inference missed aliases, Ratio values, and exact Date/DateTime/Time distinctions.
`as Quantity` assertions over FHIR values could lose the `parse_quantity`/`Quantity` shape required by downstream unit-aware comparisons.
`Message(..., 'Error', ...) as Interval<T>` wrapped strict-error expressions in type probes instead of preserving the CQLMessage call.
Dynamic FHIR `as Concept`/`as Code` assertions could collapse unknown runtime clinical values to NULL before terminology equivalence.
Property navigation from function-inlined `ParameterPlaceholder` values failed when the placeholder SQL expression was an `as`-generated SQL CASE.
Quantity comparison fallback repaired scalar optimized CTEs but initially ignored incompatible units; fallback is now gated away from JSON Quantity objects.
